title: A Salt for the Spire
premise: Sebastian Almeida steals memories for coin in the Salt Valley, the one place in the world where magic cannot follow — until prayers to the old gods begin to be answered, and one of those answers lands on him. The gods are returning through a door sealed inside a country that was erased from maps and memory generations ago, and Sebastian's stolen memories hold fragments of where that door stands. Hunted by a church that wants the gods dead and a cult that wants them awake, he gathers a found family of outcasts and follows the fragments into the vanished land. At the thirteenth turn of the moon, Sebastian must choose: reopen the door and restore the gods' corrupting power, or seal it forever by giving up every memory he has ever stolen — including his own name. He seals it, keeping only the family he made, and walks back into the valley a stranger who is finally free.
about_author: Gideon Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from families separated by borders that no longer exist. They write fantasy about inheritance, salt, and the things people refuse to forget.

chapters.title: The Taste of Other People's Years
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In the smuggler city of Vell's Landing, Sebastian lifts a memory of first love from a dying merchant for payment, showing how memory-theft works and why he never keeps what he takes. Beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Salt Lines
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He explains the valley's law: past the salt lines, magic cannot follow, which is why thieves like him live here. A client pays him to steal a memory that turns out to be a prayer — and something answers it. Beat: unease; the rules have changed.

chapters.title: What Answered
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The answered prayer manifests as a voice only Sebastian can hear, because the stolen prayer-memory lodged in him. It calls itself Ashen-Who-Waits, an old god, and asks for the rest of its name. Beat: fear mixed with a thief's curiosity.

chapters.title: The Church of the Closed Door
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Ravelle's POV. The Order that erased the old gods' country detects the answering and arrives in Vell's Landing hunting 'vessels.' Ravelle is devout but begins doubting what the Order burned. Beat: cold institutional menace with a crack of doubt.

chapters.title: A Thief, a Nun, a Debt
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Ravelle corners Sebastian; instead of arresting him, she offers a bargain — help her find the door before the Order's zealots do, or die as a vessel. Beat: reluctant alliance, mutual contempt with grudging respect underneath.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa, a mapmaker whose family drew the vanished country before its erasure, is recruited when her inherited charts prove the only guide. She resents being valued only for her dead father's work. Beat: resentment becoming purpose.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Ashen's POV (fragmentary). The god explains the moon's thirteenth turn: the door opens once per cycle, and this time the Order means to destroy it permanently. The god's memories reveal power always corrupted its worshippers. Beat: dread and moral ambiguity.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The company crosses the salt line for the first time; magic floods back into Sebastian, and the stolen memories he carries begin waking up, screaming. Beat: disorientation, wonder, and pain — the world is bigger than he was told.

chapters.title: Roadside Prayers
chapters.summary: Ravelle's POV. Villages along the road are praying again, small desperate prayers being answered badly — rain that drowns, health that consumes. Power returned without wisdom. Beat: horror at what unchecked divinity does to the humble.

chapters.title: The Zealot's Trail
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The Order's zealot wing, led by Brother Cade, burns a village that sheltered the company. Ilsa saves a child, cementing the group as family rather than allies of convenience. Beat: grief forging bonds.

chapters.title: Memories That Bite
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The stolen prayer-memories fight back; Sebastian experiences lives not his own, including a fragment showing the erased country's capital — and hints his own childhood memory was stolen from him long ago. Beat: identity crisis.

chapters.title: The Border That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Ravelle's POV. The company reaches where the vanished country should be: an empty plain the eye slides off. Only Ilsa's charts and Sebastian's stolen fragments let them perceive the border. Beat: awe and vertigo at walking into erasure.

chapters.title: Country of the Unremembered
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Inside, the erased nation persists — people who were never unmade, only forgotten, living among ruins. They remember nothing of the outside and worship the sleeping gods. Beat: bittersweet discovery; erasure spared and imprisoned them.

chapters.title: The Unforgotten King
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The last king of the erased country, kept alive by worship, reveals the truth: the gods were sealed because their power rotted everything it touched — including him. He begs them to leave the door shut. Beat: temptation inverted; the prize is poison.

chapters.title: Cade at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ravelle's POV. Brother Cade's zealots breach the border using Ravelle's own reports. Cade doesn't want the gods destroyed — he wants to take their power for the Order. Beat: betrayal of ideals; Ravelle's faith shatters entirely.

chapters.title: What Sebastian Stole
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Confronting his own stolen childhood, Sebastian learns he was born inside the erased country and carried out as a child — his whole life in the valley was someone else's design. Beat: devastating revelation; rage and grief.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Rises
chapters.summary: Ashen's POV. The moon reaches its final turn. Ashen confesses it manipulated Sebastian from the start — the prayer was bait — because a vessel must open the door willingly. Beat: betrayal within the found family; the god's desperation humanizes it.

chapters.title: Storming the Spire
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Cade seizes the spire housing the door and begins the rite to claim divine power. The company, the king's forgotten loyalists, and a wavering Ravelle assault the spire together. Beat: all-out action climax, sacrifices mounting.

chapters.title: A Salt for the Spire
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the door itself, Sebastian realizes salt — the valley's essence — can seal it permanently, but the sealing requires a vessel to pour every stolen memory into the threshold, himself included. Beat: the choice crystallizes; power refused.

chapters.title: The Giving Back
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian gives back every memory — the merchant's love, the prayers, his own name and childhood — while Ravelle holds off Cade and Ilsa anchors him with her hand and his true name spoken aloud. Beat: climax of sacrifice; identity dissolved into act of grace.

chapters.title: After the Door
chapters.summary: Ravelle's POV. The door seals; the gods sleep truly now, the erased country fades gently into peace, and Cade, emptied of his claimed power, is taken by the reformed Order. Ravelle chooses exile over promotion. Beat: cost tallied, quiet mourning.

chapters.title: A Stranger in Vell's Landing
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa brings the nameless man home across the salt line, where he can start over without a past. He doesn't remember her, but he trusts her anyway — and that, she decides, is enough to build on. Beat: resolution; found family outlasting memory itself.
